subject: Order Form + MSA: Term mechanics, auto-renew override, and transfer/sunset plan
messages:
From: Jared Blum <jared.blum@aegisbio.com>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Order Form + MSA — term language and exit ops

Hi Vivek / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is aligned on Redwood as the preferred inference partner. Legal has surfaced three sticking points tied to term/renewal mechanics and an operational plan for service sunset in the event we don’t renew. To keep momentum, can you confirm if Redwood is willing to: 

- Allow a 90-day notice opt-out for enterprise pilots earlier than the full renewal window (they want an ability to avoid a painful auto-renew on pilot accounts)
- Carve a 60-day service transfer assistance obligation in the Order Form when a customer doesn’t renew (minimum NRE hours + export of KV/keys)
- Provide a limited termination-for-convenience right on Order Forms for the first 12 months with a pro-rated service credit (they want an explicit remedy in the event business priorities change)

I’ve attached our redlines (Aegis_redlines_v2.docx) and a clean copy of the draft order form. Legal flagged that these items will determine whether procurement can sign without an escalation.

Can you confirm who on Redwood’s side will own the legal coordination? If helpful, Elena Soto (cc’d) will be the internal owner for Aegis. We’d like to close redlines in this week’s window.

Thanks,
Jared Blum
Head of Procurement, Aegis Biotech
[jared.blum@aegisbio.com]

Attachments: Aegis_redlines_v2.docx (docx), OrderForm_draft_20261205.pdf (pdf)
From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
To: Jared Blum <jared.blum@aegisbio.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 12:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order Form + MSA — term language and exit ops

Jared — thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the redlines.

Short answers up front: we can likely accommodate a structured opt-out for pilots and an export/transfer assistance clause, but termination-for-convenience with a 12-month unrestricted right is an area we need to scope with legal and product.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’m looping in Karthik (legal) to review the redlines and provide a negotiable position.
2) Kimberly (sales ops) — can you pull up the standard Order Form language we’ve used for pilot exceptions and baseline SOW commitments? I want to be sure the transfer assistance ask maps to our operational playbook.
3) Karthik — please review pages 3–5 of their redline and advise on acceptable guardrails for a termination-for-convenience (TOC) carve — e.g., limited to pilot SKUs, capped liability, and a pro-rated token/credit refund.

If we can get an internal position today, I’ll loop back to Jared with a tracked proposal and offer a quick call Tuesday to finalize.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 06 Dec 2026 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order Form + MSA — term language and exit ops

Vivek / Kimberly — reviewed Aegis’s redlines (attached) and summarized positions below. I’ve also produced a short tracked-redline doc for the MSA and Order Form we can send back (see attachment Aegis_redlines_v2.docx — note: file contains our comments in the "Redwood Response" column).

Summary of recommended positions:
- Pilot opt-out / auto-renew: agree to a 90-day opt-out window for pilot Order Forms only, provided Aegis gives notice at least 90 days before renewal AND the pilot is explicitly designated in the Order Form. We’ll add an "Opt-out for Pilot" checklist in the Order Form and a one-time administrative fee waiver only if notice is timely.

- Transfer assistance / sunset: agree to provide up to 40 engineering hours of export and handover support (documented in the SOW) plus a secure export of customer-owned artifacts (logs, model keys, and blob export). This will be a paid service for non-pilot enterprise renewals unless otherwise negotiated. We’ll include a 60-day assistance period post-termination and an explicit acceptance criteria for the export deliverable.

- Termination-for-convenience (TOC): decline an unrestricted 12-month TOC for enterprise Order Forms. We can offer a limited TOC for pilot Order Forms only, capped at 30 days’ notice and subject to a pro-rated credit of pre-paid fees (no additional damages). For enterprise deals, we propose the conventional termination-for-cause plus negotiated early-termination fees in the Order Form.

Operational asks for Sales:
- Kimberly: capture the pilot flag and associated billing code so TOC / opt-out handling can be automated at billing.
- Vivek: confirm if we want to offer a discounted transfer-assistance SKU or bill at time-and-materials for non-pilot customers.

If that aligns, I’ll draft clean redlines and propose an email that presents our positions as "compromise language" (explicitly separate pilot vs enterprise). I recommend we avoid giving a generalized TOC for any enterprise order — that’s a meaningful commercial risk.

Karthik Iyer
Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Attachments: Aegis_redlines_v2.docx (contains Redwood responses)

Two quick asks before we proceed to redline exchange:
1) Can Redwood commit to the 40-hour assistance as a credit on the first invoice for pilot customers (helps us preserve cash-flow in the pilot phase)?
2) Can we schedule a 30-minute call Tuesday at 10am PT to walk through the tracked redline and close the pilot carve?

If you can confirm (1), I’ll route internally and await the Tuesday invite.
